newsitem.title: USA: Albright plans Middle East trip by end-August.
newsitem.headline: Albright plans Middle East trip by end-August.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Wednesday she would travel to the Middle East at the end of August provided progress was made in security there.
"Provided there is some progress on security issues I am prepared to travel to the Middle East at the end of this month," Albright said in a speech prepared for delivery to the National Press Club.

Albright has been in contact with the leaders in the region by telephone and during their visits to Washington but has resisted travelling to the Middle East herself until she felt sure concrete progress could be made.

The Clinton administration has come under pressure to intervene actively as peace talks between Israelis and Palestinians remained stalled and after last week's suicide bombing in a central Jerusalem market. U.S. mediator Dennis Ross has already scheduled a trip starting this weekend.

"We now face a crisis of confidence that has put at risk past gains and rekindled old animosities," Albright said, adding that restoration of a sense of security was essential if the peace process was to be rebuilt. "The sine qua non is a mutual commitment to security against violence. This is basic. This is common sense," she said.

"The popular desire for peace is durable, resilient and strong. This is what extremists and terrorists fear the most and this is why, despite the bombing this past week and despite threats of further violence, the process of peacemaking has survived and will continue to survive," she said.
